mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.0%, market expectations for future inflation rise, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady above 5% for a dual-month period
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average preceding the trigger (t-test p > 0.05), or inflation surprises persistently exceed expectations over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting optimism about corporate hiring and productivity, which elevates S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening detected by dual-month employment surge and unemployment drop
failure_condition: In the 20-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically above the prior 10-day average (p > 0.05), or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX returns is <0.3.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months is interpreted as resilient consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations via higher earnings growth forecasts and reduces risk premia, producing a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative or flat during the three-month demand expansion, or the 20-day return is not statistically higher than the prior 10-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < previous month), suggesting supply-side constraints and muted demand, which depresses equity forward pricing and yields a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month AND CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.5% in the same month
regime_hint: Supply shock detected by simultaneous industrial production collapse and cooling inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly lower than the 30-day average prior to the shock (p > 0.05), or the event is not associated with a statistically significant increase in realized volatility over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a flight to quality in equities as investors seek safer assets, lowering equity risk premia and producing a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3 percentage points in a single month
regime_hint: Labor market weakening detected by unemployment rate spike above 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the prior 10-day average during the post-spike period (p > 0.05), or the realized volatility of SPX over the window is not significantly lower than the pre-spike average.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining labor force participation (RSAFS < previous month for two months) suggests demographic or confidence-driven labor market softening, which elevates perceived equity risk and compresses forward pricing, resulting in a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >1% each month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly lower than the 30-day average prior to the contraction (p > 0.05), or the negative effect is not statistically significant after controlling for macroeconomic variables.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time surge in consumer confidence (measured by a composite of survey indices not in the catalog, but here we proxy with a sharp drop in CPIAUCSL of >1% in a month) coincides with elevated retail sales (HOUST), indicating resilient demand that supports equity valuation upgrades and a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >1% in a single month AND HOUST increases by >3% in the same month
regime_hint: Demand shock revealed by inverted inflation and strong retail sales
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 10-day average during the shock window (p > 0.05), or the interaction between CPIAUCSL and HOUST is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO < previous month for three consecutive months) combined with stable or rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which amplifies equity discounting and produces a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >1% each month for three consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL does not decrease by >0.5% over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly worse than the 30-day average during the contraction period (p > 0.05), or the effect is driven primarily by non-supply factors (e.g., monetary policy changes).
